SELECTED PROJECTS

01EEG-Robotics Integration Platform: Jetson Vision and Cross-Platform Bridge

Real-time perception, hardware triggering and multi-device integration | UT Austin, 2025 to present

  • Built the end-to-end platform for a robotic colonoscopy study: an EEG acquisition rig linked over TCP/IP to an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super control system, a robotic endoscope with bending and feeding modules driven through a U2D2 controller and game-controller input, and a frame-grabber video chain.
  • Designed and deployed the real-time perception pipeline on the Jetson edge accelerator (USB camera, preprocessing, GPU inference optimized with TensorRT FP16 quantization, decision output), with zero dropped frames across all live operating sessions.
  • Engineered a custom TCP/IP socket client bridging a Windows-hosted BrainVision hardware amplifier and the Ubuntu/ROS 2 system, with millisecond-accurate TTL marker signaling to a third-party recording system per the hardware protocol specification.
  • Architected the ROS 2 software as separate perception and hardware-trigger nodes, with modular design, independent testing, Git version control and documentation.
  • Wrote safety-oriented control logic (confidence thresholds, sequential-state validation) so noisy sensor input cannot fire erroneous hardware triggers.
  • Profiled logged sensor and trigger telemetry to root-cause a hardware-side failure.

Tools: NVIDIA Jetson, TensorRT, ROS 2, Python, TCP/IP sockets, TTL, OpenCV, Ubuntu, Windows, Git

02Multi-Sensor Synchronization Framework

EEG, robot telemetry and insertion-depth tracking | UT Austin

  • Designed a synchronized experimental framework aligning EEG, robot telemetry and insertion-depth tracking for a robotic colonoscopy study.
  • Ran a 5-participant pilot; applied Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across 80 channel-by-depth comparisons and cross-validated results against an independent preprocessing pipeline.
  • Manuscript submitted to IEEE ICRA 2026 (under review).

Tools: Python, MATLAB, ROS 2, EEG (32-ch), spectral analysis

03Autonomous Marine Mapping Vehicle (Shumoo)

Small Hydrography Marine Boundary Boat | team build at ITN Malang, field-deployed on the Anyar River

  • Designed and built an autonomous surface vessel integrating GPS and echo-sounder hardware for real-time bathymetric mapping; field-deployed on the Anyar River.
  • Fiberglass hull carrying GPS, a thermometer and an echo sounder to record position, water temperature and depth (up to 100 m), replacing manual pole-and-diver depth measurement.
  • Built through repeated iteration: per local press coverage, the team went through about 20 failed attempts before it worked. Funded by a Dikti (Indonesian higher-education ministry) grant.
  • Covered by Indonesian press in March 2017, including interest from a Malaysian company in producing it.

Tools: Embedded hardware, GPS, echo-sounder, sensor integration

Press: Tribun Jatim coverage | Duta.co coverage
